title: The Confession of Greywater Bay
premise: When a drowned man washes up in Greywater Bay wearing clothes stolen from August Yarrow's own closet, the town's most invisible concierge becomes its most visible suspect. August's twenty years of filed confessions, favors, and overheard secrets point to one impossible conclusion: the killer is tied to the Harrow inheritance, and the only person who can identify him is a witness the whole town buried years ago. As August follows the dead man's trail through the ledgers of Greywater's founding families, she discovers the witness is alive, hidden in plain sight—and that her own late father helped stage the death to protect the Harrow fortune. In the end, August must choose between the loyalty that made her the keeper of everyone's secrets and the truth that will burn the town down; she testifies, the inheritance collapses, and she finally lets the tide take the files.
about_author: Sable Dunmore is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who spent a decade collecting the things guests confess at 3 a.m. Dunmore writes mysteries about small towns, large silences, and the people paid to keep both.

chapters.title: The Man in August's Clothes
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, August's POV. A fisherman drags a drowned stranger from Greywater Bay wearing August's missing grey overcoat and monogrammed cufflinks. The police treat her as a suspect; the town treats her as a curiosity. August, humiliated and frightened, realizes someone has dressed a corpse in her identity—and that whoever did it knew her closet better than anyone alive. Emotional beat: exposure of a woman built to be unseen.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Filed Secrets
chapters.summary: August's POV. To clear herself, August raids her private archive—the index cards, letters, and confessions she's collected as concierge. Three entries reference the Harrow estate and a fire twenty years ago that killed the heir's young wife, Lena Voss, the fire's only witness. August remembers her father burning a box the same week. Emotional beat: the past stops being background and becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: The Harrows of Saltcrest House
chapters.summary: Alternating August's POV with excerpts from old Harrow household ledgers. August takes a temporary post at the decaying Saltcrest House, now owned by matriarch Vivienne Harrow, whose grandson Edmund is set to inherit everything on his fortieth birthday. Vivienne recognizes the dead man immediately—and pays August to forget she saw. Emotional beat: temptation; August learns what her silence is worth.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: August's POV. The coroner identifies the corpse as Daniel Reeve, a former Harrow groundskeeper who supposedly drowned saving Lena Voss twenty years ago. But the body is fresh, and Reeve's pockets hold a train ticket dated last month and a key to Saltcrest's boathouse. Someone faked his death long ago—and someone killed him for real now. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Is Dead
chapters.summary: August's POV, intercut with a flashback chapter of Lena Voss's last known day. August tracks Lena's 'death': no grave, a closed casket, a death certificate signed by the town doctor—who still owes August a favor from a very bad night in 2009. The doctor admits the body in the casket was never Lena. Emotional beat: the first crack in the town's collective story, and August's first real ally.

chapters.title: Edmund's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Edmund Harrow's POV. Edmund, charming and drowning in his grandmother's expectations, reveals he's been receiving anonymous letters for months: 'Lena saw what you did.' He assumes August sent them. Their uneasy alliance forms—two people using each other to survive Vivienne. Emotional beat: seductive complicity; the reader begins to suspect Edmund is both victim and suspect.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Key
chapters.summary: August's POV. August opens the boathouse and finds Lena Voss's hidden room: twenty years of documents proving Vivienne's brother embezzled the Harrow fortune, framed Lena for it, and staged her death with the help of August's father, then the Harrows' driver. The dead man, Daniel Reeve, was blackmailing Vivienne. Emotional beat: grief and fury—August's father was complicit in the lie that shaped her whole life.

chapters.title: A Favor Repaid in Blood
chapters.summary: Vivienne Harrow's POV. Vivienne confronts August, offering the full truth as ransom: her father didn't just help stage the death—he helped kill the embezzler's accomplice, and August's inherited house was payment. Vivienne orders August to hand over the boathouse documents or be framed for Reeve's murder, and the police, bought long ago, are ready to oblige. Emotional beat: the full weight of power's corruption pressing down.

chapters.title: Lena, Rising
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. Lena Voss herself appears—alive, disguised for twenty years as the bay's reclusive ferry operator, the true author of the anonymous letters. She and August lure Vivienne and the corrupt sheriff into revealing the original murder at the boathouse, with the town's leading citizens secretly listening. Violence flares; Edmund, finally understanding his inheritance is built on a corpse, chooses to testify against his grandmother. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth collide, and truth wins at terrible cost.

chapters.title: What August Yarrow Knows
chapters.summary: August's POV, resolution. The Harrow empire dissolves in court; Vivienne is convicted, Edmund leaves town, and August's father's role is posthumously exposed, costing her the house and half the town's goodwill. On the last page, August burns her archive card by card on the shore, keeping only one: Lena's address, and an invitation to visit. Emotional beat: release—a woman who catalogued everyone's secrets finally lets herself be known.
